clue.text: Raise yak, a sprightly creature

parts.note: to jack something up is to raise it, as with a car jack
to rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering, the same as to yak

explanation.surface: Someone is told to rear a lively yak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise yak' reads like farming advice; both words are verbs giving the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American hare with long ears, famous for its bounding leaps, is a lively animal.

clue.text: A Queen song — some number one appearing in late January?

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A track by the rock band Queen, perhaps a number one hit in late January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen song' tempts as a band reference. Water-carrier signs begin around 20 January, so someone born then fits the question-marked definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born under the zodiac sign beginning around 20 January would arrive in late January.

clue.text: Take-off with singular flying tackle

indicators.note: flying means the letter flies off, leaving the word

parts.note: a take-off is a parody, a skit
S is the abbreviation for singular in grammar

explanation.surface: An aircraft take-off with singular flying equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take-off' suggests an aircraft; it is a send-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle and kit both mean the gear or equipment needed for an activity.

clue.text: Religious leader retiring to a ringing "bye bye"

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole is read right to left
ringing means the words to a surround the next piece

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for a bye, so two byes give two Bs

explanation.surface: A churchman going to bed after waving farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: A bye is a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball in cricket, abbreviated B. 'ringing' makes TOBBA, which 'retiring' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a monastery is a religious leader.

clue.text: Swede rising to meet buzzing winger's neat cross

parts.note: a bee is a buzzing winged insect

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Olaf is a typical Swedish man's name

explanation.surface: A Swede gets up to meet a fast footballer's tidy cross from the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' and 'cross' suggest football. Neat is an old word for cattle, so 'neat cross' is a hybrid of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is a hybrid of domestic cattle (neat) and American bison.

clue.text: Programmes showing after dark: a lot broadcast around one

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Lots of shows go out on air after nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges DARK and A LOT to TALKRADO, and 'around' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech-based radio output consists of programmes of phone-ins and discussion.

clue.text: Banks briefly promised backing

indicators.note: backing means the shortened word is then read from right to left
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: promised in the sense of having sworn to do something

explanation.surface: Banks, in a short statement, pledged their support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims SWORN to SWOR, and 'backing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks of oars or seats are tiers or lines set one after another, the same as lines or tiers.

clue.text: "Blooming" girl verbally abused

parts.note: Rosy is a girl's name
to cheek someone is to be insolent to them in words

explanation.surface: A girl who was flourishing suffered spoken insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbally' looks like a sound signal, but 'verbally abused' together means insulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a healthy pink glow in the face is to look blooming, flushed with health.

clue.text: Such skilful sporting shots one way to stop mocking

indicators.note: to stop means the pieces plug the gap inside the next word

parts.note: wry means drily mocking
one is I as a Roman numeral
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Skilled sporting strokes are one way to end ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' as ST (street) is a crossword staple; 'to stop' means plugging the gap in the mocking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Strokes in cricket or tennis played with strong flicking use of the lower arm are described this way.

clue.text: Ration book left half complete, suitable for recall

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance or share, a quota

indicators.note: only half complete means just the first half of the word left is written

explanation.surface: A wartime ration book is said to be half filled in and fit to be called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left half complete' gives LE, the first two of the word's four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that is worth repeating or citing is one people will recall and pass on.

clue.text: Story about idiot's miss at Hampden Park?

indicators.note: about means the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: a story can be a falsehood, a lie
an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A tale concerning a fool's failed shot at a Scottish football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a footballing failure but is a young woman. Hampden Park is Scotland's national football stadium in Glasgow, so the question mark points to a Scottish girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scots word for a girl or young woman, a miss.

clue.text: Bang on about politician's supporting Tories initially

parts.note: being pro something is supporting it
MP stands for Member of Parliament, a politician

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word Tories is used

explanation.surface: A complaint about a politician who backs the Conservative Party at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' acts as a joining word here; the pieces run in clue order once 'politician's supporting' is read as MP's PRO, placed as written: PRO, MP, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being punctual or exactly on time means arriving bang on the hour.

clue.text: Fancy brand to buy

parts.note: a make is a brand of product
to buy an idea is to accept or believe it

explanation.surface: An expensive label to purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buy' means accept as true, not purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as a noun is imagination, pretending, the stuff of imagined worlds.

clue.text: Analytic or tactful reflection concealing outrage

indicators.note: reflection means the run of letters is read in a mirror, right to left
concealing means the letters sit inside the words analytic or tactful

explanation.surface: A thoughtful or diplomatic reflection that hides a sense of outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' points to the run YTICORTA in 'analYTIC OR TActful', and 'reflection' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A shocking act of cruelty is an outrage, an appalling deed.

clue.text: American making, as it were, one roughly drawn sketch

parts.note: a whimsical coinage: someone who is yanked (pulled roughly) would be a 'yankee', as an employee is one employed
a doodle is a rough, idle sketch

explanation.surface: An American producing a hastily drawn picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' flags the invented word: the -EE ending names the person a thing is done to, so one yanked is a 'yankee'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song character's name became a nickname for any American, a Yank.

clue.text: Always around in capacity of female match-maker

indicators.note: around means the first word encloses the following pieces

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
qua is Latin for in the capacity of
Liz is a girl's name, standing for a female

explanation.surface: A woman who always pairs up couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match-maker' suggests a marriage broker; here it is the goal that levels a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal that levels the score makes the match even, so it creates a tied game.

clue.text: Keats poem done in my style

indicators.note: style used as a verb means fashion or rework, so the letters are restyled

explanation.surface: A Keats poem written the way I would write it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' rearranges DONE IN MY, eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The long Romantic poem by John Keats opens 'A thing of beauty is a joy for ever'.

clue.text: Guilt beckons for gallivanting literary lady

indicators.note: gallivanting means roaming about, so the letters of the two words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman of letters feels guilt calling her to go out and enjoy herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gallivanting' rearranges GUILT and BECKONS, twelve letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The term was used, often mockingly, for an intellectual or literary woman, after an eighteenth-century salon.

clue.text: Send up fool about to get the bird

parts.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high in the air
to lark is to fool about

explanation.surface: Someone mocking a clown gets jeered off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' suggests mockery and 'get the bird' booing; both mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is a songbird famed for singing as it rises.

clue.text: Just pass the pickle!

definitions.meaning: to get through a test by the narrowest margin
a pickle is an awkward predicament or fix

explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' looks like food; it means a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed narrowly is to squeak by, and an awkward fix is a tight spot.

clue.text: One leading church funds summer treat

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
CE is the Church of England
lolly is British slang for money or funds

explanation.surface: A person heading a church raises money for a summertime outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' simply places I before the rest. An ice lolly is the British name for a frozen flavoured treat on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen fruit treat on a stick is eaten on hot days, a typical sunny-season snack.

clue.text: Effect of shooting Communist spy

parts.note: Red is a standard nickname for a Communist
a private eye is a detective, someone who spies

explanation.surface: The consequence of gunning down a Communist agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns, but it means taking photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flash photography can make pupils glow red in a photo, a flaw of taking pictures.

clue.text: Gravestone may have this, see

definitions.meaning: headstones often carry the letters for 'rest in peace' followed by a preposition
a see is a bishop's diocese, here a Yorkshire cathedral city

explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a bishop's seat; the cathedral city in North Yorkshire is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A North Yorkshire cathedral city is a bishop's diocese, and also reads as a tombstone phrase.

clue.text: Tunic made in seconds from ends of silky material: some waxed, woven gauze

indicators.note: seconds from ends means the letter standing second from the end of each following word is taken

parts.words: silky material: some waxed, woven gauze

explanation.surface: A tunic is run up in moments from silky fabric, some of it waxed, plus woven gauze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds from ends of' keeps only the second-to-last letter of each word: silKy, materiAl, soMe, waxEd, wovEn, gauZe; every other letter goes. 'made in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: This long shirt or tunic is worn with loose trousers across South Asia.

clue.text: I expand novel with insertion of page

definitions.text: I expand novel with insertion of page

indicators.note: with insertion of means a letter is put inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The supplement speaks: I enlarge a book by adding a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges I and EXPAND to APENDIX, and 'with insertion of' puts P inside. The whole clue is what an end section of a book might say about itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplementary section at the back of a book adds material to it, expanding the text.

clue.text: River just not long enough for a duck

indicators.note: just not long enough means the word falls one letter short, losing its last

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A stream barely too short to suit a waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a duck is a score of zero, so 'duck' is not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman's score of zero is a duck in cricket, the same as nothing.

clue.text: One of the old folk from sea front in Eastbourne

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: front in means the first letter of Eastbourne

explanation.surface: A pensioner arriving from the seafront at Eastbourne, a south-coast resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old folk' suggests elderly people at a seaside town; it is an ancient people. Eastbourne is an English seaside resort popular with retired people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medes were an ancient people of Iran, so one of them belongs to an old nation.

clue.text: Making fire again on heather to keep warm

indicators.note: to keep means the outer pieces hold the next word inside them

parts.note: re means on or concerning
ling is a name for common heather
kind means warm-hearted

explanation.surface: Lighting a fire again on heather moorland to stay warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warm' is the adjective kind-hearted, not heat; 'to keep' places it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting something again, as one restarts a fire, is the literal sense.
